syllabus_extract: Optical holography basic principle, procedure for setting up construction and re-construction, laser, interferogram advantages disadvantages and application
specific_objectives: 19.1.5.1 Trainee will be able to explain the optical holography and acoustic emission inspection

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Demonstration of holographic setup using laser source, beam splitter, and recording medium; safety precautions regarding laser eye protection and alignment stability; instructor supervision of beam path and recording process.
intro_questions: What is the fundamental difference between a photograph and a hologram?
Name one type of laser commonly used in non-destructive testing.
Why is coherence essential for interferometry?

topics: Role of laser coherence and monochromaticity
development.content:
Basic principle of optical holography
Role of laser coherence and monochromaticity
Interference pattern formation
Recording medium requirements

Procedure for setting up construction
Laser alignment and beam splitting
Reference and object beam configuration
Interferogram advantages and disadvantages

Procedure for re-construction of hologram
Light source requirements for reconstruction
Image formation and viewing angles
Applications in NDT

summary_questions: Explain how the interference pattern stores three-dimensional information.
List two advantages and two disadvantages of using interferograms in inspection.
Describe the critical steps required to successfully reconstruct a holographic image.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief report comparing the setup requirements for optical holography and acoustic emission inspection, highlighting key differences in data acquisition.
